name: GitHub
description: Connect repositories, issues, pull requests, and GitHub Projects.

methods.whenToUse: Use the provider-hosted connection for the quickest setup.
methods.guidanceMd: Create a fine-grained token limited to the repositories agents should use.

methods.whenToUse: Authorize a dedicated Paperclip OAuth App for repositories, issues, and personal or organization Projects.
methods.guidanceMd: Register an operator-owned GitHub OAuth App with Paperclip's exact displayed callback URL and expiring user tokens. Enter the public client ID and select the client secret from Paperclip's company-scoped secret store. Review GitHub's consent screen yourself. Connecting does not grant agents access, activate discovered operations, or start synchronization.

credentialFields.label: Client ID
credentialFields.placeholder: Paste the public OAuth client ID

warnings: By default Paperclip requests only read:project and public_repo: Projects are read-only and only public repositories are reachable. Full repo and project scopes (broad read and write access to every private repository available to the authorizing account; OAuth Apps cannot select individual repositories at consent) are requested only when you explicitly opt in to private repositories.
The project scope permits reading and updating personal and organization Projects. Repository and organization policies can still restrict access.
offline_access requests expiring access tokens and refresh support; Paperclip must verify the actual response before saving a connection.
GitHub consent is separate from Paperclip agent access and approval for each write operation. No import or agent run starts merely by connecting.
